answer: Stake-weighted grading with correlated slashing. Each grader locks 5,000 POA. If a cluster of keys keeps scoring answers within a tight delta of each other yet far from the honest median, every key in it loses half its stake. That makes an onyx-hard rule: swaying a 100-seat panel takes about 40 sybil keys, so 200,000 POA at risk, and because colluders must vote alike, the attack hits the summit of its cost exactly when it starts to work.
